findings.problem: The proof states the composite-is-quasi-iso fact, then states the target `QuasiIso (Φ.map …)` in full and proves it with the iff `quasiIso_iff_comp_left …).mp inferInstance`. Mathlib has the one-directional lemma `quasiIso_of_comp_left`, which takes `[QuasiIso φ]` and `[QuasiIso (φ ≫ φ')]`. It gives exactly this step without restating the long `Φ.map (mapBifunctorMap …)` term or building an iff and projecting `.mp`. The same long term is written three times.
findings.proposed_change:
Replace lines 27–33 with a single step that names the composite and uses the one-directional lemma:
```
  have hcomp : QuasiIso ((scalarForgetTotalIso k A B P Q).hom ≫
      Φ.map (mapBifunctorMap f g (bifunctor k A B) (ComplexShape.down ℕ))) := by
    rw [← h]
    infer_instance
  have : QuasiIso (Φ.map (mapBifunctorMap f g (bifunctor k A B) (ComplexShape.down ℕ))) :=
    quasiIso_of_comp_left (scalarForgetTotalIso k A B P Q).hom _
  exact (quasiIso_map_iff_of_preservesHomology _ (forgetField k (A ⊗[k] B))).mp inferInstance
```
The isomorphism `(scalarForgetTotalIso …).hom` is already a quasi-isomorphism by instance, as the current `.mp inferInstance` relies on. The `Φ` binding can also be dropped from the last `have`, so the long target term is not repeated.
findings.benefit: The 'cancel a quasi-isomorphism on the left' step now reads as one named lemma application. It no longer restates the long term or goes through an iff and `.mp`, so the argument is shorter and its structure is clearer.
